description: Golden enforcement-notice → obligation links (HLD v2 §4.7). Each case is the text of a published outcome, the registry rows (source_key, clause_ref) live at the time, optional extra instrument aliases (what the DB adds from a source's short name / instrument), and the set of registry rows the notice cites as breached. The deterministic linker (app.clhear.l7.enforcement.link_text) is scored on precision over all predicted links; gate >= 0.90. Recall is reported. Nothing may link without a printed citation.

cases.notice: The FCA has fined Northbridge Capital Ltd £4,650,000 for breaching SYSC 6.1.1R and SYSC 6.3.1R between January 2019 and March 2022.
Final Notice: breaches of SYSC 4.1.1R, 4.1.2R and 6.1.1R.
The firm breached Principle 11 by failing to deal with the regulator in an open and cooperative way. It was fined £1,100,000 on 14 May 2024.
The FCA found that the firm breached regulations 28(2) and 33 of the MLRs 2017 by failing to conduct customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence.
Penalty of £2,300,000 for failings under regulation 19 of the Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017.
Monetary penalty notice: infringement of Article 5(1)(f) of the UK GDPR and Article 32 of the UK GDPR (security of processing).
FINRA fined the firm $350,000 for violating FINRA Rule 3110(a) and FINRA Rule 2010 (Letter of Acceptance, Waiver and Consent No. 2021069876501).
Without admitting or denying the findings, the firm consented to the sanctions and to the entry of findings that it violated FINRA Rules 3110 and 4511.
The SEC's order finds that the broker-dealer violated Exchange Act Rule 15l-1 (Regulation Best Interest) and 17 CFR 248.30 by failing to act in retail customers' best interest.

SEC Charges Investment Adviser With Misleading Clients. The adviser agreed to pay a $1.2 million civil penalty and disgorgement of $800,000 plus prejudgment interest on 30 April 2024 (Release No. IA-6592).
On 3 July 2023 the regulator publicly censured Beta Bank plc for failings under rule 2 of the Synthetic Principles and SYN PRIN 4.
The firm breached COBS 9.2.1R and COBS 9.2.2R (suitability).
FINRA found that the firm failed to establish a reasonable supervisory system in violation of FINRA Rule 3120.
